concepts.def: The physical components of a computer system, such as the processor, memory, storage devices and input and output peripherals.
Software that manages and supports the computer itself, including the operating system, utility programs and program translators.
Software that performs tasks for the end user, such as word processors, spreadsheets and web browsers, rather than managing the machine.
A translator that converts a whole high-level program into object code in one pass before execution, reporting all syntax errors together.
A translator that analyses and executes a high-level program line by line each time it runs, without producing a stored object-code file.
An electronic component implementing a Boolean operation such as AND, OR or NOT, combining binary inputs to produce a binary output.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Computer Systems — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Computer Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Computer Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is system software?
options: A spreadsheet package
An operating system
A web browser
A photo editing app

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler translates the whole program before execution; an interpreter translates and executes line by line
An interpreter produces a standalone executable file
A compiler executes code without translating it
They are two names for the same translator
High-level language into pseudocode
Machine code into assembly language
Assembly language mnemonics into machine code
One high-level language into another

mcqs.q: An AND gate outputs 1 only when:
options: Both of its inputs are 1
At least one input is 1
Both inputs are 0
Exactly one input is 1

mcqs.q: Does an interpreter produce an executable file that can be run later?
options: No - an interpreter translates and executes the source code line by line each run; it is the compiler that produces a stored object-code executable.
Yes - interpreters save a machine-code file just like compilers.
Yes - interpreters convert programs into assembly files on disk.
Yes - anything with a user interface is application software.

mcqs.q: Is the operating system an example of application software?
options: No - the operating system is system software: it manages hardware, memory, files and processes, providing the platform on which applications run.
Yes - the OS is just another app installed on the computer.
Yes - anything with a user interface is application software.
OR works on numbers while XOR works on letters.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1; XOR outputs 1 only when exactly one input is 1, so they differ when both inputs are 1.
They are the same gate with two different names.
OR works on numbers while XOR works on letters.
Yes - anything with a user interface is application software.
